title: putting a name to it
subtitle: what words can do for a feeling

steps.prompt: what did the study of couples find about self-compassion?
steps.answer: partners described people higher in self-compassion as more caring and accepting. it's a link, not a cause.

steps.text: some feelings arrive as a fog: big, with no edges.
has saying what a feeling was ever helped?

options.label: yes, a bit
options.reply: good. that fits what researchers have seen.

options.label: not really
options.reply: that's fine. it doesn't work every time, or the same way for everyone.

options.label: never tried it
options.reply: then this is a nice time to try.

steps.text: in a brain-imaging study, people who put a feeling into words showed quieter activity in the amygdala, which responds to emotional images, than people who didn't.
steps.evidence: moderate (a small imaging study; later work points the same way)

steps.text: that doesn't mean the feeling goes away. it can mean it takes up a bit less room.
